articles.excerpt: Scaffold a minimal module with deterministic registration and verify that Magento discovers it.
articles.content:
Scaffold a minimal module with deterministic registration and verify that Magento discovers it.

Problem: Scaffold a minimal module with deterministic registration and verify that Magento discovers it. Teams often ship a quick patch that passes in developer mode but fails DI compilation, cache invalidation, or store-scoped configuration in staging.

Outcome: You will implement and verify this pattern on Adobe Commerce / Magento Open Source 2.4.x using the MaheshDave_DevTools module (app/code/MaheshDave/DevTools, Composer package maheshdave/dev-tools).

Before you start

  • Confirm the exact Commerce version and PHP runtime used by the target environment.
  • Work in a disposable local or staging environment and commit the current state before changing configuration or schema.
  • Check edition and installed-module availability; Cloud-only and B2B capabilities are not universal.

Implementation example

File or area: registration.php

The following focused example illustrates the core configuration or code shape. Treat names and values as module-specific, and connect it to the supporting classes and configuration required by your implementation.

<?php
use Magento\\Framework\\Component\\ComponentRegistrar;
ComponentRegistrar::register(ComponentRegistrar::MODULE, 'MaheshDave_DevTools', __DIR__);

Keep the example inside a module-owned file. Do not edit files under vendor/ or generated code; those changes are overwritten by dependency installation or code generation.

Supporting implementation

Minimal etc/module.xml that matches the registration name:

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd">
    <module name="MaheshDave_DevTools" setup_version="1.0.0"/>
</config>

Run the checks

Use these commands as a starting verification sequence:

bin/magento module:status MaheshDave_DevTools
bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento cache:flush

Run Magento CLI commands as the filesystem owner and adapt paths, locales, service endpoints, and test suites to the deployment. If a command is unavailable in your version, inspect bin/magento list and the matching release documentation.

Debugging and failure modes

  • Change is not detected: verify module registration, directory and XML names, XML schema, module sequence, and cache state.
  • Compilation or DI errors: read the first exception, confirm constructor types and preferences, then run DI compilation in a non-production build.
  • Works locally but not in staging: compare edition, patch level, PHP extensions, enabled modules, store scope, environment configuration, and generated static assets.
  • Behavior differs by store view: test default, website, and store-view scope explicitly.

Production-readiness checklist

  • Validate input and authorization at the service/controller boundary, not only in the UI.
  • Bound memory, response size, query count, retries, and execution time for batch or integration work.
  • Log enough context to diagnose failures, but redact tokens, credentials, payment data, and customer personal information.
  • Add automated tests for success, invalid input, empty results, permissions, and partial failure.
  • Document rollback and recovery verification.

Key design note: Keep module name, directory, and module.xml name identical; commit registration.php and etc/module.xml together.

Conclusion

A reliable Magento implementation is more than a snippet: it needs correct framework wiring, explicit version assumptions, observable failure behavior, and a repeatable verification path. Start with the smallest change, test it against realistic data, and record the expected result so maintainers can recognize regressions.

Can I deploy this without running the checks?

No. Run the verification commands in staging on the same Commerce patch level as production, then promote through your normal release process.

Compare enabled modules, environment variables, and build hooks. Cloud restricts some filesystem writes—keep customizations in app/code or shared mounts documented for your project.

Start with var/log/exception.log and the first stack trace line, then confirm module sequence, cache type, and store scope.

Implementation example

Supporting implementation

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\\DevTools\\ViewModel;

use Magento\\Framework\\View\\Element\\Block\\ArgumentInterface;

class ProductNote implements ArgumentInterface
{
    public function getNoteHtml(int $productId): string
    {
        return $this->escaper->escapeHtml(
            (string) $this->noteProvider->getForProduct($productId)
        );
    }
}

articles.title: How to Remove a Fastly VCL Snippet Using CLI
articles.excerpt: Remove a blocking Fastly VCL snippet via the Fastly API or CLI when Magento admin is unreachable—backup, clone, delete, validate, activate, and purge safely.
articles.content:
When a custom Fastly VCL snippet blocks Magento admin access (for example Maintenance_Trigger), you can remove it safely using the Fastly API and curl — without Magento admin or the Fastly web UI.

This guide covers:

  1. Backing up existing VCL snippets
  2. Removing a specific snippet
  3. Activating the new VCL version
  4. Purging Fastly cache

Prerequisites

ItemDescription
Fastly Service IDFastly dashboard → Service configuration, or Magento Cloud FASTLY_SERVICE_ID
Fastly API TokenFastly dashboard → Account → API tokens (snippet edit + purge permissions)
Snippet nameExact name, e.g. Maintenance_Trigger
Toolscurl, bash, optionally python3 or jq

Important: Fastly version rules

You cannot edit an active (locked) version directly.

Workflow:

  1. Clone the active version
  2. Delete the snippet on the cloned draft
  3. Validate the new version
  4. Activate the new version
  5. Purge cache

Step 1 — Set environment variables

export FASTLY_SERVICE_ID="YOUR_SERVICE_ID_HERE"
export FASTLY_API_TOKEN="YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE"
export SNIPPET_NAME="Maintenance_Trigger"
export BACKUP_DIR="./fastly-vcl-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
echo "Backup directory: $BACKUP_DIR"

Step 2 — Get the active VCL version

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/active" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

Extract the active version number:

export ACTIVE_VERSION=$(grep -o '"number":[0-9]*' "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
echo "Active version: $ACTIVE_VERSION"

Alternative (Python):

export ACTIVE_VERSION=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json'))['number'])")
echo "Active version: $ACTIVE_VERSION"

Alternative (jq):

export ACTIVE_VERSION=$(jq -r '.number' "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json")
echo "Active version: $ACTIVE_VERSION"

Note: Use -o to save JSON. Do not use curl -w with JSON files — it appends HTTP_STATUS:200 and breaks JSON parsing.

Step 3 — Backup all VCL snippets

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/snippet" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

List all snippet names:

grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

Confirm target snippet exists:

grep -i "$SNIPPET_NAME" "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

Step 4 — Backup the specific snippet

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/snippet/$SNIPPET_NAME" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/${SNIPPET_NAME}-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/${SNIPPET_NAME}-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

Save VCL content to a .vcl file (optional):

python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os

backup_dir = os.environ["BACKUP_DIR"]
snippet = os.environ["SNIPPET_NAME"]
version = os.environ["ACTIVE_VERSION"]
path = f"{backup_dir}/{snippet}-active-v{version}.json"

data = json.load(open(path))
out = f"{backup_dir}/{snippet}.vcl"

with open(out, "w") as f:
    f.write(data.get("content", ""))

print(f"Saved: {out}")
PY

Step 5 — Clone the active version

curl -sS -X PUT -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/clone" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json"

Set the new draft version:

export NEW_VERSION=$(grep -o '"number":[0-9]*' "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
echo "New draft version: $NEW_VERSION"

Step 6 — Delete the snippet from cloned version

curl -sS -X DELETE -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/snippet/$SNIPPET_NAME" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/delete-snippet-response.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/delete-snippet-response.json"

Verify snippet is removed:

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/snippet" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-new-v${NEW_VERSION}.json"

grep -i "$SNIPPET_NAME" "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-new-v${NEW_VERSION}.json" \
  || echo "Snippet removed successfully"

Step 7 — Validate VCL before activation

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/validate" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/validate.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/validate.json"

Confirm status is ok before activating. Do not activate if validation fails.

Step 8 — Activate the new VCL version

curl -sS -X PUT -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/activate" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/activate.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/activate.json"

Step 9 — Purge Fastly cache

curl -sS -X POST -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/purge_all" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/purge.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/purge.json"

Step 10 — Verify admin access

Open Magento admin in a private/incognito window:

https://your-domain.com/admin

Complete one-shot script

Save as remove-fastly-snippet.sh:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

export FASTLY_SERVICE_ID="YOUR_SERVICE_ID_HERE"
export FASTLY_API_TOKEN="YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE"
export SNIPPET_NAME="Maintenance_Trigger"
export BACKUP_DIR="./fastly-vcl-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

echo "==> 1) Get active version"
curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/active" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

export ACTIVE_VERSION=$(grep -o '"number":[0-9]*' "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
echo "    Active version: $ACTIVE_VERSION"

echo "==> 2) Backup all snippets"
curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/snippet" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

echo "==> 3) Backup target snippet"
curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/snippet/$SNIPPET_NAME" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/${SNIPPET_NAME}-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

echo "==> 4) Clone version"
curl -sS -X PUT -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/clone" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json"

export NEW_VERSION=$(grep -o '"number":[0-9]*' "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
echo "    New version: $NEW_VERSION"

echo "==> 5) Delete snippet"
curl -sS -X DELETE -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/snippet/$SNIPPET_NAME" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/delete-snippet-response.json"

echo "==> 6) Validate"
curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/validate" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/validate.json"
cat "$BACKUP_DIR/validate.json"

echo "==> 7) Activate"
curl -sS -X PUT -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/activate" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/activate.json"

echo "==> 8) Purge cache"
curl -sS -X POST -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/purge_all" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/purge.json"

echo "Done. Backups saved in: $BACKUP_DIR"

Make executable and run:

chmod +x remove-fastly-snippet.sh
./remove-fastly-snippet.sh

Alternative: Fastly CLI

If Fastly CLI is installed:

export FASTLY_API_TOKEN="YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE"
export FASTLY_SERVICE_ID="YOUR_SERVICE_ID_HERE"

Backup:

fastly service vcl snippet list \
  --service-id "$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID" \
  --version active

fastly service vcl snippet describe \
  --service-id "$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID" \
  --version active \
  --name Maintenance_Trigger

Delete (auto-clones if needed):

fastly service vcl snippet delete \
  --service-id "$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID" \
  --version active \
  --name Maintenance_Trigger \
  --autoclone

Activate and purge:

fastly service version activate \
  --service-id "$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID" \
  --version latest

fastly purge \
  --service-id "$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID" \
  --all

Rollback

Reactivate the previous version if something goes wrong:

curl -sS -X PUT -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/activate"

Purge cache again:

curl -sS -X POST -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/purge_all"

Troubleshooting

FileNotFoundError: active-version.json

Backup file was not created. Re-run Step 2 and confirm BACKUP_DIR is set in the same shell.

echo "BACKUP_DIR=${BACKUP_DIR:-NOT_SET}"
ls -la "${BACKUP_DIR:-missing}"

JSONDecodeError: Extra data

curl -w appended HTTP_STATUS:200 after JSON. Re-fetch cleanly:

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/active" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

Or fix existing file:

head -n 1 "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json" > /tmp/active-version.clean.json
mv /tmp/active-version.clean.json "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

Validate JSON:

python3 -m json.tool "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

Invalid credentials

{"msg":"Provided credentials are missing or invalid"}

Check FASTLY_API_TOKEN and regenerate if needed.

Service or snippet not found

{"msg":"Record not found"}

Verify FASTLY_SERVICE_ID and snippet name (case-sensitive):

grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

Admin still blocked after removal

# Purge again
curl -sS -X POST -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/purge_all"

Also check on the server:

# Magento Cloud SSH
ls -la var/maintenance.flag
bin/magento maintenance:status

Test admin in incognito/private browser window.

Auth header for all requests:

-H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN"

Best practices

  • Always back up before deleting snippets
  • Validate VCL before activation
  • Keep the backup directory until admin access is confirmed
  • Never commit API tokens to git
  • Use incognito/private window when testing admin after changes

Applicable to Adobe Commerce / Magento 2 with Fastly CDN (fastly/magento2 module).

Key takeaways

  • Active Fastly versions are immutable—always clone before deleting snippets.
  • Validate VCL before activation; keep JSON backups until admin access is confirmed.
  • Pair CDN changes with Magento maintenance checks (var/maintenance.flag) when admin stays blocked.

articles.title: Design GraphQL Resolvers That Avoid N+1 Catalog Loads
articles.excerpt: Batch product and attribute loads inside service classes so Storefront GraphQL queries stay within latency budgets under load.
articles.content:
Problem: A resolver that calls ProductRepositoryInterface::get() for every cart line or category tile multiplies database and Elasticsearch work—GraphQL looks convenient but can amplify N+1 patterns.

Outcome: You will structure resolvers and services so related entities load in bounded batches with explicit field selection.

Before you start

  • Capture a baseline query with Blackfire, New Relic, or Magento profiler on a representative category or cart query.
  • Confirm whether catalog reads hit Elasticsearch or MySQL in your index configuration.

Anti-pattern vs batching service

// Anti-pattern inside a field resolver
foreach ($items as $item) {
    $product = $this->productRepository->getById((int) $item['product_id']);
}
// Batch in a dedicated service used by the resolver
$ids = array_column($items, 'product_id');
$products = $this->productCollectionFactory->create()
    ->addFieldToFilter('entity_id', ['in' => $ids])
    ->addAttributeToSelect(['name', 'sku', 'price']);
$map = [];
foreach ($products as $product) {
    $map[(int) $product->getId()] = $product;
}

Supporting implementation

Expose only the fields you need in GraphQL schema to prevent accidental deep trees:

type StoreProductNote {
    product_id: Int!
    note: String
}

Run the checks

bin/magento cache:clean graphql
# Run the same GraphQL query twice; compare query count in profiler

Common mistakes

  • Loading full product models when a lightweight DTO suffices.
  • Calling repositories from nested resolvers without a DataLoader-style batch.
  • Ignoring store view and customer group when building collection filters.

Conclusion

GraphQL performance is a service-layer design problem. Batch early, select fields explicitly, and measure under realistic catalog size.

FAQs

Should I disable GraphQL fields instead?

Remove unused fields from schema and resolvers before micro-optimizing SQL—clients cannot over-fetch fields you do not expose.

articles.title: Verify Payment Webhooks with Idempotency and Signature Checks
articles.excerpt: Accept gateway webhooks only after signature verification, persist idempotency keys, and avoid double invoice or cancel races.
articles.content:
Problem: Payment gateways may deliver success, failure, and retry events out of order. Without verification and idempotency, Adobe Commerce can cancel an order after capture or create duplicate invoices.

Outcome: A webhook controller pattern that validates signatures, deduplicates events, and delegates order state changes to sales services.

Implementation example

File or area: webhook front controller + service

public function execute(): ResultInterface
{
    $raw = (string) $this->request->getContent();
    if (!$this->signatureValidator->isValid($raw, $this->request->getHeaders())) {
        return $this->json(['message' => 'invalid signature'], 401);
    }
    $event = $this->json->unserialize($raw);
    $key = (string) ($event['id'] ?? $event['transaction_id'] ?? '');
    if ($key === '' || $this->idempotency->isProcessed($key)) {
        return $this->json(['status' => 'ignored']);
    }
    $this->paymentHandler->apply($event);
    $this->idempotency->markProcessed($key);
    return $this->json(['status' => 'ok']);
}

Supporting implementation

Persist idempotency keys in a small declarative table or cache with TTL longer than gateway retry windows:

<table name="maheshdave_devtools_webhook_event" resource="default" engine="innodb">
    <column xsi:type="varchar" name="event_key" length="128" nullable="false"/>
    <constraint xsi:type="primary" referenceId="PRIMARY">
        <column name="event_key"/>
    </constraint>
</table>

Security considerations

  • Reject unsigned payloads; rotate webhook secrets through config—not code commits.
  • Return generic 401/403 without leaking internal order IDs.
  • Log correlation IDs, not full card or wallet payloads.

Run the checks

bin/magento setup:upgrade
# Replay the same webhook payload twice — second call must not change order state

Conclusion

Treat webhooks like untrusted input until verified. Combine signature checks, idempotency storage, and sales service APIs to stay aligned with payment reality.

FAQs

Can I fix a canceled-but-paid order with SQL?

Only as a last-resort support runbook after confirming capture in the gateway; prefer admin or service APIs and document audit comments.

articles.title: Use React Server Components Patterns in Modern Storefront SPAs
articles.excerpt: Apply React 19 / RSC-inspired boundaries in headless storefronts: keep data fetching on the server, stream UI, and hydrate only interactive islands.
articles.content:
Problem: Shipping the entire catalog API surface to the browser increases bundle size and exposes integration details. Teams need a clear split between server-fetched data and client interactivity.

Outcome: A practical pattern for Adobe Commerce headless or custom React storefronts using server loaders and client islands—without assuming a specific vendor starter kit.

Prerequisites

  • Node.js LTS and a React 18+ or 19 project with a server runtime (Next.js App Router, Remix, or custom SSR).
  • Storefront GraphQL or REST credentials scoped read-only where possible.

Server loader example

// app/product/[urlKey]/page.tsx — server component
export default async function ProductPage({ params }: { params: { urlKey: string } }) {
  const product = await getProductByUrlKey(params.urlKey);
  if (!product) notFound();
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{product.name}</h1>
      <AddToCartButton sku={product.sku} />
    </main>
  );
}

Client island with explicit boundary

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';

export function AddToCartButton({ sku }: { sku: string }) {
  const [pending, setPending] = useState(false);
  async function add() {
    setPending(true);
    try {
      await fetch('/api/cart/items', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ sku, qty: 1 }),
      });
    } finally {
      setPending(false);
    }
  }
  return <button disabled={pending} onClick={add}>Add to cart</button>;
}

Performance and security

  • Keep customer tokens and admin URLs off the client bundle; proxy cart mutations through your BFF.
  • Cache product queries at the edge with keys that include store code and customer group when pricing differs.

Run the checks

npm run build
npm run start
# Lighthouse: confirm reduced JS on product route vs fully client-rendered baseline

Conclusion

Adopt server-first data loading for catalog pages, hydrate only interactive widgets, and measure bundle and TTFB after each change.

FAQs

Does Adobe Commerce ship RSC out of the box?

PaaS storefronts vary (Luma, Hyvä, headless). This article describes patterns you apply in your chosen React framework, not a core Commerce feature flag.
